items.title: NBCC among 5 stocks showing White Marubozu Pattern
points: On November 2, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 6% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.
A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.
The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow.
It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close.
The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Sabarmati-style Yamuna riverfront ‘could worsen flood risks’ in Delhi, environmentalists and others warn
points: A proposed 52-km Yamuna riverfront development project in Delhi on the lines of Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati riverfront has drawn opposition from a coalition of environmentalists, former water ministry officials, researchers and citizen groups.
The letter argued that the Sabarmati model cannot be replicated along the Yamuna without accounting for the fundamental differences between the two rivers.

The objections come days after the Delhi government, on October 21, announced that it was initiating the process of signing a memorandum of understanding with the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL) for the project.
The proposed development will span 52 km in two phases – from Palla to Wazirabad in the first, and from Wazirabad to Kalindi Kunj in the second.

They also pointed out that most polluting drains have been diverted away from the Sabarmati riverfront stretch, an arrangement that cannot be replicated on the Yamuna, which flows through several states downstream of Delhi.

Data from 58 of the 59 monitoring stations showed that eight were in the severe category on Tuesday morning, including Bawana, Narela and Punjabi Bagh.
The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) classifies an AQI of 0–50 as “good”, 51–100 as “satisfactory”, 101–200 as “moderate”, 201–300 as “poor”, 301–400 as “very poor” and 401–500 as “severe”.
NASA satellite data detected 1,561 farm fires in Punjab and Haryana between October 1 and November 2, 1,406 in Punjab and 155 in Haryana.

items.title: 2 brothers held for killing cheetah cub near Kuno park, gun found
points: The Madhya Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has arrested two brothers for allegedly killing a 19-month-old cheetah cub, officially known as Kuno Nirva Gaurav or KNG-22, outside the Kuno National Park and recovered the licenced double-barrel gun they used…

According to an STF officer, the male cub (KNG-22) was rescued in an injured condition from compartment No. 748 of Sheopur forest division on October 25, however it died during treatment two days later.
The four-member STF arrested Bhagwan Singh, a resident of Morena district, on October 31.
Both were remanded in two-day judicial custody on October 31 and produced before the court again on Monday, which sent them to judicial custody, a senior forest department official said.
During interrogation, Singh allegedly confessed that on October 24, he and Pritam Singh had gone to the forest to hunt a wild boar.
A case was registered against both under sections 9 and 51 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (Amended 2022).

items.title: Activists raise concern over Supreme Court order on green firecrackers, traders lament stock availability
points: Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital.

In 2019, when only green crackers were allowed and several months were given to prepare for implementing it, Delhi still saw the decision being openly flouted and also there was a lack of stock in many shops.
Later, the Delhi government moved to a complete ban, including green firecrackers, for a few months around Diwali, but that too was flouted on a large scale.
Last year, the Supreme Court passed a order similar to this year, lifting the ban temporarily to allow green firecrackers to be burst for a fixed window of time for two days during Deepavali.

Even after the ban was reimposed after Deepavali last year, people continued to burst firecrackers for marriages, concerts and everything else in Delhi,” said Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist.
